package_info.package_manager: npm (also distributed via CDN and bundled in CMSes)
package_info.why_malicious: CKEditor 4 versions prior to 4.16.1 are vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks (CVE-2021-33829) due to improper sanitization of HTML comments containing the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword. Attackers can inject specially crafted payloads that exploit this flaw, bypassing intended protections and enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution in the context of users editing or viewing content.

execution_context.file_location: rich text content field (e.g., blog post, CMS page, admin editor)
required_permissions: none (attacker needs ability to submit content)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views or edits the content in CKEditor 4, the editor processes the injected HTML containing a malformed comment with the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword, which bypasses sanitization; as a result, the tag with an onerror handler is rendered and executed, leading to arbitrary JavaScript execution in the user's browser.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload uses a malformed HTML comment and the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword to evade CKEditor 4's sanitization logic, allowing the injection of an tag with an inline JavaScript event handler.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User-supplied HTML should be sanitized to prevent script execution, especially within comments containing reserved keywords; the sanitization fails, allowing XSS.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of HTML comments and tags is common, but not with reserved keywords or inline event handlers intended for code execution.
key_indicators: Presence of the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword in user-submitted HTML comments
Malformed HTML comment closure (e.g., --!> instead of -->)
Inline JavaScript event handler (onerror) in tag within user content

execution_context.file_location: rich text content field (e.g., blog post, CMS page, admin editor)
required_permissions: none (attacker needs ability to submit content)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views or edits the content in CKEditor 4, the editor processes the HTML containing a nested 'cke_protected' keyword within a malformed comment, which bypasses single-pass sanitization; this results in the tag with an onerror handler being rendered and executed, causing arbitrary JavaScript execution in the user's browser.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload exploits recursive or nested use of the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword to evade single-pass sanitization, enabling the injection of executable JavaScript.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Sanitization should recursively remove or encode all instances of reserved keywords, but the implementation only removes one layer, allowing nested payloads to persist.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for nested reserved keywords in user content; such patterns are only used for evasion.
key_indicators: Nested or recursive use of the 'cke_protected' keyword in HTML comments
Malformed HTML comment closure (e.g., --!> instead of -->)
Inline JavaScript event handler (onerror) in tag

required_permissions: none (attacker needs ability to submit content)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views or edits the content in CKEditor 4, the editor processes the HTML containing a doubly-nested reserved keyword and malformed comment closure, which bypasses sanitization; this exposes the tag with an onerror handler, resulting in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the user's browser.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload demonstrates that the sanitization logic fails to handle multiple or malformed nested reserved keywords, allowing the injection of executable JavaScript.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Sanitization should handle all forms of reserved keyword injection, including complex nesting and malformed comments, but fails in this case.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Such complex nesting of reserved keywords and malformed comments is not legitimate in normal user content.
key_indicators: Malformed HTML comment closure (e.g., --!> instead of -->)
Inline JavaScript event handler (onerror) in tag

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits specially crafted HTML payload containing the reserved 'cke_protected' keyword and malformed HTML comments to a CKEditor 4 instance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in the application database or content field.

attack_chain.action: Another user (or the attacker) opens the vulnerable content in CKEditor 4 in edit mode.
attack_chain.leads_to: CKEditor 4 processes the content, fails to sanitize the payload, and renders the malicious tag.

attack_chain.action: The browser interprets the malformed comment, exposes the tag, and executes the onerror JavaScript handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary JavaScript executes in the victim's browser (XSS), leading to account takeover, credential theft, or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: User-supplied content containing the 'cke_protected' keyword in HTML comments
Malformed HTML comments (e.g., --!> instead of -->) in user content
Presence of tags with inline JavaScript event handlers (e.g., onerror) in stored content
Nested or recursive use of 'cke_protected' within HTML comments
file_indicators: Rich text fields or database entries containing <!--{cke_protected}--!> or nested variants such as <!--{cke{cke_protected}_protected}--!> or <!--{cke_{cke_protected}protected}--!>
Content with patterns in user-submitted or stored HTML
network_indicators: N/A (XSS is a client-side attack; network indicators may only appear if the injected payload attempts exfiltration via HTTP requests)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan user-submitted and stored HTML content for the presence of the 'cke_protected' keyword within HTML comments, especially with malformed comment closures (e.g., --!>) or nested/recursive patterns. Flag any content containing tags with inline event handlers such as onerror. Monitor CKEditor 4 instances for attempts to inject or render such payloads, and alert on any execution of suspicious JavaScript in the context of the editor. Automated detection should focus on identifying malformed or nested reserved keywords and inline event handlers in user content.
